gen-dafont-groovy-fs-synonym: Funky and friendly, Groovy leaves the c nearly shut and spaces its lowercase loosely. Synonym runs a plain, steady stripe of ink with generous curve openings, so paragraphs of it glide along without a snag.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-almendra: Loose, friendly, funky: Groovy has no stroke contrast at all, just loosely tracked lowercase. Almendra, a classic serif with a deep lowercase midsection, brings a dignified, bookish weight that Groovy lacks.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-bree-serif: Friendly in spirit, Groovy grabs attention with its engraver-style cut, a single depth with no deeper spots. And Bree Serif, a classic serif with outsized lowercase, does the literary, refined work of carrying the text.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-port-lligat-slab: Friendly, funky, loosely spaced: Groovy's r, n and m have arches matching their stems. Port Lligat Slab, a serif with porthole-wide counters and open-ended curves, supplies the literary, traditional grounding.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-quando: Quando sets sparse, widely spaced letters around a tall middle zone in every word, which gives it a bookish, traditional voice. Groovy brings the pipe-cleaner fun; Quando does the reading.
gen-dafont-groovy-outfit: Outfit feels clean and approachable, its curves finishing well before they close, with no swelling or thinning anywhere. Groovy's nearly closed letters make that openness stand out.
gen-dafont-groovy-plus-jakarta-sans: Groovy leaves the c almost closed, just a narrow slit. Plus Jakarta Sans, a sans-serif with monoline strokes and curve endings kept well apart, feels modern and precise beside that funky, closed-up heading.
gen-dafont-groovy-sora: Precise and geometric, Sora lets no curve swell at its corners. Groovy, funky and loosely tracked, has a narrow slit where the c almost closes, which makes Sora's widely parted curves feel generous.
gen-dafont-groovy-space-grotesk: Loose, funky, almost-closed letters lead the way. Space Grotesk, a sans with counters that breathe like a hollow reed and ribbon-like constant-width strokes, keeps paragraphs moving at an easy pace.
gen-dafont-hammerhead-fs-amulya: Hammerhead is industrial and authoritative, a plain unmodulated outline with a wide-open e that never looks pinched. Amulya, a contemporary sans with generous gaps in its curves, lets long paragraphs flow easily.
